articleTitle: The picture quality implications of low bit-rate terrestrial television
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Developments in Terrestrial Broadcasting for the UHF Band
abstract: The author seeks to determine the likelihood of HDTV broadcasting on a terrestrial channel using low bit-rate picture coding techniques. A two-stage approach to scene-dependent quality characterisation accounts first for statistical variation of criticality in typical television, and then determines viewers' tolerance of occasional picture distortion. The importance of a hierarchical coding and decoding environment is discussed, with the basic ideas of subband coding. A consideration of graceful degradation of quality in adverse transmission conditions includes the principles which could make this a feature of all-digital television transmission.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The transmission of digital television in the UHF band using orthogonal frequency division multiplexing
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Developments in Terrestrial Broadcasting for the UHF Band
abstract: This paper is concerned with a very robust means of transmitting data, which also has excellent interference rejection properties. Descriptions are given of an experimental transmitter with a fast Fourier transform processor, and a receiver with a digital signal processing array.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Developments in Terrestrial Broadcasting for the UHF Band
abstract: The author gives a potted history of Channel 5, from a technical point-of-view, going over the various unique characteristics of this transmission network, its transmitter frequency plan, and potential interference with domestic video equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Enhanced terrestrial television; the domestic receiver
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Developments in Terrestrial Broadcasting for the UHF Band
abstract: The author draws attention to challenges confronting the domestic TV receiver designer in an age of new terrestrial PAL signals on established or hitherto unused channels, and digital (orthogonal FDM) transmission of totally unrelated format, as well as the European Community EMC Directive. An opinion is expressed in favour of either another signal-processing 'set-top box', or a modular receiver with features selected by the viewer at the point of sale.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The use of UHF broadcasting spectrum for services ancillary to broadcasting
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Developments in Terrestrial Broadcasting for the UHF Band
abstract: Planning the use of television spectrum within the UK is complex, requiring a detailed knowledge of existing and proposed television coverage. This paper outlines the procedures adopted for planning a range of ancillary services, from conventional low power analogue devices used at outside broadcast locations to complex digital links transmitted from permanent sites.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
